newsitem.title: FRANCE: Five bombs hit Corsica, no one injured.
newsitem.headline: Five bombs hit Corsica, no one injured.

text.p: Suspected Corsican separatists exploded five small bombs early on Sunday at banks and tax collectors' offices on the Mediterranean island, police said. No one was hurt.

Two other bombs failed to detonate in the worst night of bombings in more than a month. The tourist island has been battered by thousands of explosions over the past two decades by guerrillas pushing for more autonomy from mainland France.
No one claimed responsibility for the series of blasts just after midnight, each of about 300 grams (10 oz) of explosives.
In Ajaccio in southern Corsica, bombs caused slight damage at branches of Credit Agricole, Societe Generale and Credit Lyonnais banks.
In northern Corsica, blasts wrecked doors and smashed windows in public revenue offices in Pietrabugno and Vescovato.
